paragraphs: Children in care in Suffolk are looked after by Suffolk Fostering Service, run by Suffolk County Council, and by the independent agencies shown above. The council's statement of purpose for 2023-24 records that at the start of March 2023 it had 383 approved fostering households, counting mainstream, family and friends and short-break Link carers, and that 510 of its 964 children in care (52.9%) lived with those in-house carers.

The same document says more than half of Suffolk's children in care are 11 or older, yet fewer people come forward to look after them, and when the county joined Foster East in May 2024 its cabinet member for children named teenagers as the particular need. Suffolk is a coastal county with a port at Felixstowe, and a Local Government Association case study describes the arrival of around 120 unaccompanied children a year; the council looks to place those under 16 with foster carers and has set up support groups for both its own carers and agency carers around the county.

The council offers short-term and long-term care, emergency and short-break care, remand care through its PACE scheme, early permanence, therapeutic fostering, kinship care and Link care, which gives disabled children short stays with another family. Approval for a new carer usually takes about six months from the point an application is accepted, or about four months for carers who already foster.

Suffolk pays on a five-level scheme, set out in full on our Suffolk pay page. For 2026-27 every council carer receives a weekly child allowance in four age bands, from £187 for a child under five to £274 for a 16 or 17-year-old, and from Level 2 a weekly fee on top that rises with the level, so the total for one child runs from £332 to £798 a week. There are four extra weeks of allowance a year for birthdays, holidays and festivals, up to 21 paid nights of short breaks, a 24-hour out-of-hours service and membership of the Fostering Network and the Suffolk Foster Carer Association.

Agencies set their own fees and support, so speak to the council and two or three of the services above and compare them. If you live in or near the county town, the Ipswich page has more on the area, and the Norfolk, Essex and Cambridgeshire pages list services across the county's borders.
